subject: Dynamic-length elementary items (maximum length)
notes: kb/Work PB463 LANDED - the A.1 item 62 determination is STATED and IMPLEMENTED. 8.5.1.10.1 makes the maximum size of a dynamic-length elementary item "the smallest of" three candidates and A.1 item 62 makes the third of them - "the maximum permitted by the implementor" - required AND documented; 13.18.19.4 GR2 makes it the whole answer when no LIMIT phrase is written. WiseOwl COBOL provides 1,073,741,791 characters (0x3FFFFFDF) for every dynamic-length elementary item, alphanumeric or national: the CARRIER's own ceiling, since the item IS a native System.String whose maximum length is that value - the same "the carrier's headroom IS the implementor maximum" reading CobolDynTable<T>.MaxOccurrences already records for a dynamic-capacity table. A LIMIT phrase below it is the maximum size; one above it cannot raise the maximum and is REPORTED (COBOL2027, a warning - 13.18.19.3 bounds integer-1 only when a dynamic-length-structure-name is written too, SR4, so the entry is legal source). The second candidate never applies: the PREFIXED phrase rides a dynamic-length-structure-name, refused by COBOL1562. ONE producer computes it (CobolDynString.MaxSizeOf) and DataItem.DynMaxSize carries it, so the value cannot differ between the binder, the emitters and the runtime; DynamicLengthTests.ImplementorMaximum_IsTheNumberPublishedInConformanceSection7 reads the number back out of the section 7 row in both published spellings, so the determination and the constant cannot drift apart. Before this landing the item had no maximum at all and the section 7 register said only that a branch was unreachable - a determination about code nobody had checked, which is how a SET SIZE past 2**32 came to wrap to its low bits.
